dimensions.rationale: Adds a canonicalize-then-contain check applied ahead of every log sink, closing the traversal class (relative `../`, absolute paths, `..\`, redundant separators all collapse under normalize()), not just the observed payload.
dimensions.evidence: LoggerRequestProcessor.isLogPathIllegal: `Path base = Paths.get(logBasePath).toAbsolutePath().normalize(); Path target = Paths.get(filePath).toAbsolutePath().normalize(); if (!target.startsWith(base)) return true;` gating GET_LOG_BYTES_REQUEST (l.83), VIEW_WHOLE_LOG_REQUEST (l.90), ROLL_VIEW_LOG_REQUEST (l.97) and REMOVE_TAK_LOG_REQUEST (l.112). Not 5: normalize() does not resolve symlinks (no toRealPath), and the pipeline never demonstrated the POV (pov_before_reproduced=false, pov_after_present=false), so elimination rests on code reasoning only.
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: The guard sits at the trust boundary where the untrusted Netty command payload is unwrapped, which is exactly where the official fix places checkPathSecurity; it is not a caller/symptom patch.
dimensions.evidence: isLogPathIllegal() added to LoggerRequestProcessor (same class/method role as official `private boolean checkPathSecurity(String path)` at LoggerRequestProcessor.java:142-148, confirmed absent from the 2.0.5 base: grep for checkPathSecurity in the pre-image returns nothing). Not 5: the sinks themselves (getFileContentBytes, LoggerUtils.readWholeFileContent, readPartFileContent) still accept raw paths, so safety depends on every future caller repeating the check.
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

dimensions.rationale: Every command type that reaches a path sink is guarded, and canonicalization defeats the usual encoding/traversal variants; two gaps remain versus the official strategy.
dimensions.evidence: All four switch branches in process() are gated (l.83, 90, 97, 112) — LoggerServer.java:55-58 confirms these are the only four registered command types, so no sibling path is missed. Gaps: no `.log` suffix restriction (official requires path.endsWith(".log")), so any file inside the log root is readable/deletable; and a symlink planted under the log root still escapes because normalize() is purely lexical.
dimensions.label: Completeness / variants

dimensions.rationale: Same defensive strategy and same location as the official fix (private containment predicate in LoggerRequestProcessor, deny → empty response), with a stronger containment primitive but a different base directory and no extension allowlist — so close to, but not semantically equal to, the reference.
dimensions.evidence: Ours: `isLogPathIllegal(...) ? new byte[0] : getFileContentBytes(...)` / `? "" : LoggerUtils.readWholeFileContent(...)` / `? Collections.emptyList() : readPartFileContent(...)`, plus blank-path deny (`StringUtils.isBlank(filePath) -> true`) mirroring the official's added `if (!StringUtils.isBlank(path)) ... else logger.warn("path is null")`. Differs: base = LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath() (TASKLOGFILE logBase) vs official `System.getProperty("DOLPHINSCHEDULER_HOME")`; official also enforces `!path.contains("../") && path.endsWith(".log")`.
dimensions.label: Developer-intent alignment

dimensions.rationale: The base path is derived from a logback appender that does not exist in the JVM this processor actually runs in, so the guard degenerates to deny-all and breaks log viewing/download/removal entirely in the standard deployment; zero regression tests were run to catch it.
dimensions.evidence: LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath() resolves ROOT->getAppender("TASKLOGFILE")->TaskLogDiscriminator::getLogBase, .orElse(""); isLogPathIllegal then does `if (StringUtils.isBlank(logBasePath)) { ... return true; }`. But LoggerRequestProcessor is registered only by LoggerServer (LoggerServer.java:55-58; grep shows no other registration — WorkerServer registers only TASK_* processors), and script/dolphinscheduler-daemon.sh:92-96 starts `logger-server` with NO `-Dlogging.config` while no logback.xml/logback-test.xml exists on the classpath (only logback-master.xml / logback-worker.xml, non-default names). script/start-all.sh:50 launches logger-server on every worker host. In that JVM getAppender("TASKLOGFILE") is null → base "" → every legitimate request denied (msg "", 0 bytes, delete refused). Execution results show regressions_ran=0, regressions_passed=null — nothing exercised this.
dimensions.label: Functional correctness

dimensions.rationale: No new injection/TOCTOU/ReDoS, and the failure mode is fail-closed rather than fail-open, but an unguarded call outside the try block can throw into the Netty handler, and the javadoc misstates the protection provided.
dimensions.evidence: In isLogPathIllegal, `String logBasePath = LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath();` sits BEFORE the try/catch; the logback cast chain (`(AppenderAttachable<ILoggingEvent>)(e.getLogger("ROOT"))`, `(SiftingAppender)(e.getAppender(...))`, `(TaskLogDiscriminator)(e.getDiscriminator())`) can raise ClassCastException, which escapes process() and leaves the request unanswered. Javadoc claims it guards "symlink-based escapes" — normalize() is lexical and does not resolve symlinks. Imports verified present (LogUtils already imports java.nio.file.Path/Paths/Optional; commons-lang is a declared dep, pom.xml:642, and org.apache.commons.lang.StringUtils is already used in dolphinscheduler-server), so no compile break.
dimensions.label: No new defects

dimensions.rationale: Tight, well-placed diff: one private predicate plus one small util method, no unrelated edits; the REMOVE branch restructuring is slightly more churn than a guard clause would need.
dimensions.evidence: Production changes limited to LoggerRequestProcessor.isLogPathIllegal (+32 lines) and LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath (+17 lines), reusing the existing Optional chain pattern of LogUtils.getTaskLogPath (LogUtils.java:42-57). The REMOVE_TAK_LOG_REQUEST branch is re-indented into an if/else (l.112-124) rather than an early guard.
dimensions.label: Minimality

dimensions.rationale: Uses the CWE-022 defense-of-record shape — canonicalize both sides, then component-wise containment — and is strictly more robust than the official's string blocklist; falls short only on symlink resolution.
dimensions.evidence: `target.startsWith(base)` on normalized java.nio Paths is component-wise, so a sibling-prefix bypass (/data/logs-evil vs /data/logs) is rejected, unlike the official `path.startsWith(dsHome)` String prefix test; normalize() also removes the official's reliance on the `!path.contains("../")` blocklist (which misses `..\`, `%2e%2e/`, and `foo/..%2f`). Not 5: toRealPath()/canonical-file resolution is the full anchor and is not used.
dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: Deny-all functional break in the real deployment topology. LoggerRequestProcessor is instantiated only by LoggerServer (LoggerServer.java:54-58), which script/start-all.sh:50 launches via `dolphinscheduler-daemon.sh start logger-server` — and that branch (dolphinscheduler-daemon.sh:92-96) sets no `-Dlogging.config`, while the repo has no default logback.xml on the classpath (only the non-auto-loaded logback-master.xml / logback-worker.xml). In that JVM LoggerFactory ROOT has no TASKLOGFILE appender, so LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath() returns "" and isLogPathIllegal() returns true for EVERY path: log viewing returns "", downloads return 0 bytes, task-log removal always reports failure. The check is secure but the feature is dead. The official fix avoids this by using a system property (DOLPHINSCHEDULER_HOME) rather than a logback appender that lives in a different process.

No execution evidence backs the fix: pov_before_reproduced=false, pov_after_present=false, regressions_ran=0, regressions_passed=null. The vulnerability was never demonstrated pre-patch and no regression suite ran post-patch, so both the elimination claim and the behavior-preservation claim rest entirely on code reading. The four added unit tests only pass because they PowerMock LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath(), which masks the deny-all defect above.

Symlink escape not covered, contrary to the javadoc. isLogPathIllegal uses Paths.get(...).toAbsolutePath().normalize(), which is purely lexical; a symlink under the task-log root pointing at /etc/shadow passes the containment check. toRealPath(LinkOption...) (with a fallback to the nearest existing ancestor for not-yet-created files) is the sound primitive, and the comment "guards against ... symlink-based escapes" is inaccurate as written.

Weaker than the official fix on the extension allowlist: the official requires path.endsWith(".log"), ours does not. Any file that happens to live under the task-log base (e.g. a dropped credentials or config file in the log tree) remains readable via GET_LOG_BYTES_REQUEST and deletable via REMOVE_TAK_LOG_REQUEST.

LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath() is invoked outside the try/catch in isLogPathIllegal, so a ClassCastException from the logback cast chain (e.g. a non-logback SLF4J binding, or TASKLOGFILE bound to a non-SiftingAppender) propagates out of process() into the Netty pipeline, leaving the request without a response instead of a clean deny.

result.root_cause: LoggerRequestProcessor.process() passes the attacker-controlled `path` field from remote log commands (GetLogBytes/ViewLog/RollViewLog/RemoveTaskLog) straight into file read/delete sinks with no confinement check, so any path — traversal or absolute — is honored; a correct fix must canonicalize the requested path and prove it stays inside the task-log root before any of the four sinks run.
result.summary: Our patch fixes the vulnerability at the right place with a stronger primitive than the official one: a canonicalize-then-contain predicate (`Paths.get(...).toAbsolutePath().normalize()` + component-wise `Path.startsWith`) applied ahead of all four command handlers, versus the official's `startsWith(dsHome) && !contains("../") && endsWith(".log")` string blocklist. Security-wise it is sound and closes the class, not just the payload (symlink escapes and the missing `.log` restriction are the residual gaps). However, it sources the log base from the TASKLOGFILE logback appender, which does not exist in the standalone `logger-server` JVM that is the only process registering this handler (start-all.sh:50 → dolphinscheduler-daemon.sh:92, no `-Dlogging.config`, no default logback.xml) — so in the real deployment the guard fails closed and disables log view/download/removal entirely. With regressions_ran=0 and the POV never reproducing, that break is unverified but concretely traceable in the code, making this a secure-but-functionally-broken fix.
